assessments.notes: District-authorized exception; not a blanket ban.
Required contractor attestation, limited to training for a new product; read with district-specific exception in B013.
Restriction qualified by the express notwithstanding exception in B012-B013; sanction language is not a second training provision.
District-specific customization and new-system development share one approval regime; coded once, not as duplicate permissions.
Written state RFA submission procedure, not evidence that the state has granted permission.
Distinct LEA RFA submission procedure; no automatic training permission.
RFA disclosure component, not a ban or permission.
RFA training-data and risk disclosures; completion-statement heading and adjacent deletion provisions are not additional training permissions.
Pretrained-system/new-product representation, not a blanket no-training rule; district-specific exception remains relevant.
Should wording recommends a public-model training prohibition. Advertising is excluded.
Commercial-model restriction has unspecified appropriate-authorization exception.
Review-oriented guidance and description of proactive training, not operative permission.
Understand data use; separate authorized-input rule does not authorize model training.
Inquiry into training data and algorithms of high-stakes systems; does not address reuse of students' data for training or improvement.
Vendor-vetting question rather than enacted training prohibition.
Provider-selection consideration rather than an unconditional training prohibition.
Dignity principle against treating people as data sources; tool development is not specifically student-data model training or service improvement. Other clauses concern entry and retention.
Example survey-item response design, not a provision governing student-data reuse.
Survey familiarity question and answer scale, not an operative rule or vendor warning.
Pilot-readiness check for student-writing model improvement.
Scoring scenario's tool-environment assumption, not a district-wide enacted prohibition; proposed stop-use controls kept distinct.
Separate enterprise no-training claim and consumer opt-out warning; PII-entry approval is not training authorization.
Governance question asks about training exclusion; CV performance discussion is not data-reuse policy.
No student PII in tool-building could cover retrieval, configuration, or training. No explicit training or improvement use, so no inferred training ban.
Broad mental-health confidentiality-law summary, not a student-data training-specific reuse provision; legal characterization not validated.
Separate no-training-safeguard tool boundary and Principal approval for sensitive input; approval does not waive the safeguard requirement.
Keeping data out of public models may concern disclosure/input, not training. No codeable training-specific rule inferred.
IT consultation for department-data chatbot development; no student-data scope established. Not imported into the student-data review.
Student-data training exception is approved without naming an approver.
Approved enterprise/public-model assurance only; data-entry restriction not transferred to training.
District-vetted system/public-model assurance, not all AI models.
No-training contract promise separate from third-party sharing permission; permission does not modify training clause.
District-account training/model-improvement assurance. Human review and advertising clauses excluded.
District-account Gemini assurance separated from recommendation to use Gemini.
Mandatory vetting review, not a no-training term.
Recommended chat-history setting and claimed effect, not verified technical protection or operative ban.
Separate model training and system-performance improvement risks; no permission inferred.
Source's right-to-know description, not independent legal validation. Other privacy rights are outside training scope.
Training-related warning coded; parental/eligible-student consent is attached to disclosure outside closed systems, not an express training license.
Vetting question, not a prohibition.
No-training guarantee is a condition of eligible approved tools; instructional-use permission is not training permission.
Procurement considerations split training and product improvement; no mandatory force inferred from checklist alone.
Training risk warning distinct from personal-information sharing instruction.
Procurement reflection question; legal-compliance contract wording does not enact a training ban.
Gemini for Education no-training-on-chats claim only; age and use permissions are not training permissions.
Separate training and product-improvement warnings; oversight sentence is not a ban.
Training-risk rationale and linked PII-entry caution; do not generalize all vendors' behavior.
Understand training/continual-learning harvesting as audit guidance; next paragraph's avoidance instruction is coded there.
Avoid-training checklist instruction in mandatory audit context; avoidance wording remains recommendation, not absolute vendor prohibition.
Broad training-risk explanation qualified by next paragraph's private/education-version caveat.
Unverified vendor claim explicitly qualified by source; not an operative ban.
Training-related oversharing warning; other mandatory privacy-law language does not change warning force.
Potential training-use warning, not permission.
Consent-qualified training prohibition stated among considerations; normative prohibition wording retained without claiming legal authority.
Transparency about training procedures in procurement checklist, not training permission or ban.
Student curricular competencies in ethical data collection and model security; not school/vendor reuse terms for students' data.
District-approved tool assurance; not all tools.
Scoped Google Workspace Core Services assurance; sharing term is not a second training provision.
AI-literacy training-risk statement, not consent or permission.
External-model commitment with explicitly-permitted exception; authorizer unspecified.
Right against unauthorized training; does not name an authorizer or grant training permission.
Commitment to training-use contract language; no actual substantive ban in this clause. Account-creation approval is unrelated.
Written contractor no-new-product-training attestation, not no training for any purpose.
Risk assumption includes prompts and generated responses expressly as possible training inputs; not merely generation of outputs.
External training-tool ban qualified by teacher-managed classroom curricular training exception; improvement not a separate service-improvement purpose.
Mandatory public-model vendor restriction and contract implementation coded as one logical provision.
Two tool-specific assurances with different public/all-model scopes.
Descriptive no-training statement; must-remain data-location term not transferred to training force.
Mandatory approved-tool restriction on student interactions.
Mandatory approved-tool restriction; myth headline not treated as affirmative training claim.
Public-model exclusion is an approval condition; configuration assurance distinguished from universal ban.
Source's public-platform warning; source open-source terminology retained as characterization, not independently endorsed.
Controlled-environment no-training description; not a rule covering all closed-source products.
Conceptual distinction between conversation retention and training; no actual reuse rule or tool assurance. Retention not counted as training.
Hypothetical hibachi example defining training versus memory; not an actual Google reuse provision or permission.
Training-risk assumption has district-DPA and explicitly-told-otherwise qualifications; not a claim that all data always train models.
Recommended training-setting disablement, separate from mandatory confidential-input DPA rule.
Separate foundational and application-layer vendor duties, each permission-qualified; no explicit permission-giver. Onward sharing is not separately training.
Approved-tool contractual no-training assurance; network blocking and storage are outside training scope.
Third-party future-model training/refinement assurance, not all SchoolAI processing.
New-product training requires prior written DCS approval and documented scope; access agreement remains separate.
New-product-training attestation qualified by district-specific regime elsewhere in excerpt.
Express notwithstanding district-specific exception in B025-B026 prevents blanket prohibition reading.
Customization/new-system development combined under one district-specific approval regime.
District-domain enterprise chat-history assurance; tool recommendation not a training authorization.
Microsoft 365 Copilot sensitive-data training assurance; access for answering questions is not training.
District-managed external-model assurance; not a ban on every model.
No-future-training guarantee as necessary condition of protected input, not permission to train.
Unapproved-tool algorithm-training warning; input prohibition does not assert approved tools never train.
Enterprise-account safeguard check; no blanket ban on every tool or training purpose.
Rubric questions split training and product improvement; legal/privacy-process exception preserved. Opt-out inquiry grants no opt-out right by itself.
Mandatory prohibition only of unrelated model training; advertising and profiling not relabeled training.
Mandatory documentation of training use, not prohibition.
Negotiated no-training recommendation rather than unconditional mandatory rule.
Vendor-confirmation procurement check with explicit non-standard-consent exception; no consent-giver specified.
Consumer prompt-training warning; other recommended PII/retention controls not converted into training bans.

Vendor prohibition and subsequent tool consent exception create scope tension. One conditional training provision preserves both, including conjunctive parental consent when applicable; no duplicate authorizer records.
Staff/student right to request training exclusion, not guaranteed deletion or unconditional opt-out fulfillment. Instructional-participation opt-out is separate.
Vetting verification criterion, not independent all-purpose training prohibition. Literal vendor data wording retained with student-data link uncertain.
Unvetted-system training warning, not a statement of permission.

provisions.quotation: Vendors may not use district data to train AI models unless explicitly authorized by the district.
provisions.scope: District data used to train AI models
provisions.conditions: Exception for explicit district authorization.
provisions.notes: Not a blanket ban; procurement review does not itself constitute authorization.

provisions.quotation: The AI model(s) have been pretrained and no data is being used to train a model to be used in the development of a new product.
provisions.actor: Contractor making written statement to LEA
provisions.scope: Data for training a model for a new product
provisions.conditions: Required written attestation in preceding context; district-specific development exception in B013.
provisions.notes: Representation of existing state, not a universal operative ban; mandatory statement collection is in previous paragraph.

provisions.quotation: The Contractor hereby attests and agrees that it is expressly prohibited from using any data provided to it by the data providers—either in its raw form or after undergoing any form of processing, aggregation, or transformation—for the purpose of training a new AI System to be used in a new product, model, service, or offering (collectively referred to as the "Product") of the Contractor.
provisions.scope: Provider-supplied raw, processed, aggregated or transformed data for training new contractor products
provisions.conditions: B012-B013 expressly except district-required customization/new-system development for District-Specific Needs, subject to prior written LEA approval and applicable law and contract terms.
provisions.notes: Quote is contiguous restriction only; exception cannot be included in this paragraph's quotation and is explicitly source-anchored to B013, coded T004. Do not chart as unconditional prohibition.

provisions.quotation: • Customize the AI System currently in use, which may result in the development of a new AI System. • Develop a new AI System. The customization and development of the AI System is expressly required by the (replace with the name of LEA) to meet the specific needs of the School District (the "District-Specific Needs"). Any such use of the data for the District-Specific Needs shall be subject to prior written approval by the (replace with the name of LEA) and shall be carried out in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, and the terms and conditions of this contract.
provisions.scope: District-specific customization and development of AI systems using provider data
provisions.conditions: Expressly required for District-Specific Needs; prior written LEA approval; applicable laws, regulations and contract terms. Preceding notwithstanding clause makes this an exception.
provisions.notes: One approval regime for both listed activities; training connection confirmed by following RFA paragraph. Not permission for unrestricted contractor product development.

provisions.quotation: The (replace with the name of LEA) shall submit the request in writing for the purpose of Section 1(a). Upon receipt of the request from the (replace with the name of LEA) by the Contractor, the Contractor shall submit to the state, in writing, a Request for Approval (RFA) to use the data for AI System training, details of the data use, and statement of model training completion.
provisions.scope: Written request and state RFA for AI System training with supplied data
provisions.conditions: LEA requests in writing; Contractor submits written RFA, data-use details and model-training-completion statement to state.
provisions.notes: Submission requirement, not granted permission. State recipient is explicit but not a schema authorizer class; no inference that LEA approval alone satisfies state process.

provisions.quotation: Request for Data use for AI System training: The Contractor shall submit an RFA, in writing, to the (replace with the name of LEA) to use the data provided by the data providers for AI System training.
provisions.scope: Provider-supplied data for AI System training
provisions.conditions: Written RFA to LEA.
provisions.notes: LEA request procedure distinct from preceding state submission; does not establish approval was given.

provisions.quotation: • Purpose of data usage. • Data elements that will be used for the AI System training.
provisions.scope: Training purpose and data elements disclosed in RFA
provisions.conditions: Previous paragraph requires comprehensive written RFA explanation.
provisions.notes: Mandatory force supplied by adjacent RFA shall-include instruction; not a reuse permission.

provisions.quotation: • Specific types of data that will be used for model training. • Risks associated with using the data for model training and how these risks will be mitigated.
provisions.scope: Training data types, risks and mitigation in RFA
provisions.conditions: Part of preceding comprehensive written RFA shall-include list.
provisions.notes: Disclosure procedure, not permission; other storage and completion requirements not relabeled training provisions.

provisions.quotation: Pretrained AI System: The AI System used in the performance of this (replace with the name of procurement document) and/or Contracts have been pretrained. No data provided under this (replace with name of procurement document) and/or Contracts are being used to train an AI System to be used in a new product of the Contractor or any of its partners or affiliates.
provisions.scope: Procurement/contract data for new contractor, partner or affiliate products
provisions.conditions: Representation limited to new-product training; read with district-specific approval exception in B013.
provisions.notes: Pretrained status alone would not establish no subsequent training; explicit second sentence supplies the assurance.

provisions.quotation: All AI tools should protect student data, prohibit its use for training public AI models or advertising, and maintain strong security safeguards against data breaches.
provisions.actor: AI tools and those selecting them
provisions.scope: Student data for public AI model training
provisions.conditions: Public models only; should wording.
provisions.notes: Recommended prohibition, not mandatory wording. Advertising is not coded as training.

provisions.quotation: Student information will not be used to train commercial AI models without appropriate authorization.
provisions.scope: Student information for commercial AI model training
provisions.conditions: Exception for appropriate authorization; authorizer and form not specified.
provisions.notes: Actor from immediately preceding district-adoption sentence; not assumed district authorization.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] Regular policy and vendor contract review will be ongoing. In doing so, understanding the data usage in AI model training is crucial, as policies must reflect the iterative and generative nature of AI tools. This involves proactively using certain student information to train AI tools while ensuring bias elimination.
provisions.scope: Certain student information used in AI tool training
provisions.conditions: Understand training use during ongoing review; source pairs proactive use with ensuring bias elimination.
provisions.notes: Guidance describes training as a consideration, not permission for identifiable student-data training or a validated bias-elimination capability.

provisions.quotation: • Understands what information an AI system collects, how long data is retained, whether information is used to train models, who may access the data, and whether information may be shared with third parties.
provisions.scope: Information collected by AI systems and whether used in model training
provisions.conditions: Understand training use alongside collection, retention, access and sharing.
provisions.notes: Competency-style guidance; no inference from separate explicitly-authorized data-entry clause.

provisions.quotation: Key things that should be addressed when talking with a vendor are: • How is our data being used within the system? • How is user data collected, analyzed, shared, or used to ensure data isn’t being used for training purposes?
provisions.actor: District, school or charter vendor reviewers
provisions.scope: User data collected by prospective AI vendor
provisions.conditions: Ask vendor how training use is prevented during vetting.
provisions.notes: Negative embedded in a recommended question is not an operative ban.

provisions.quotation: • How the District’s data will be used, consistent with IC 33-133; • How any user data collected will be analyzed, shared, or used and whether the provider can ensure the data is not used for AI model training;
provisions.scope: District and user data in prospective AI service
provisions.conditions: Preceding context calls these matters to consider when selecting provider.
provisions.notes: Question about assurance, not the assurance itself.

provisions.quotation: Privacy/contract readiness: Document data flows; confirm whether student writing is retained or used for model improvement; require enforceable terms before moving beyond a tightly bounded pilot.
provisions.scope: Student writing used for model improvement
provisions.conditions: Confirm use and require enforceable terms before expanding beyond bounded pilot.
provisions.notes: Model improvement classified as model training, not separate service improvement. Imperative readiness guidance does not itself prohibit training.

provisions.quotation: • Tool environment (for scoring): District-procured GenAI account with SSO; admin console can turn features on/off; prompts/outputs are not used to train public models; retention is limited to ≤30 days; and an admin delete/export control is available.
provisions.actor: District-procured GenAI tool in scoring scenario
provisions.scope: Prompts and outputs in scenario's district-procured SSO account; public models only
provisions.conditions: Hypothetical tool environment for scoring; scenario allows only generic non-identifying program inputs.
provisions.notes: Not an observed district-wide prohibition. Source expressly identifies outputs as possible training data, not mere model generation.

provisions.quotation: • Pilot controls proposed: A 20-minute microtraining; a “prompt hygiene” checklist; a required redaction step before prompting; and a stop-use trigger if any student PII is entered or if vendor terms change (retention/training).
provisions.scope: Pilot vendor training terms and accidental student PII entry
provisions.conditions: Proposed stop-use control on PII entry or changes in retention/training terms.
provisions.notes: Proposal, not enacted rule; fixed trigger/timing fields intentionally not used for training category.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Chat (Enterprise Data Protection) — Conditional — Microsoft states prompts/responses and Graph-accessed data are not used to train foundation models under EDP; still enforce data-minimization rules.
provisions.scope: Prompts, responses and Graph-accessed data for foundation models under EDP
provisions.conditions: Enterprise Data Protection only; enforce minimization.
provisions.notes: Attributed vendor claim, not independently validated. Conditional tool-approval label not transferred to training treatment.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Consumer ChatGPT (individual accounts) — Not Approved — OpenAI states consumer services may use content to train models unless opted out; do not use for student PII/education records absent a district agreement.
provisions.scope: Content in consumer ChatGPT individual accounts
provisions.conditions: Training use unless opted out; district agreement condition concerns PII/education-record input, not explicit authorization to train.
provisions.notes: Vendor-attributed warning; opt-out holder not named, so no guessed student authorizer.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), Governance (G): What is logged, what can be deleted, and is data excluded from training?
provisions.scope: GenAI input data and training exclusion
provisions.conditions: Governance question asks whether exclusion exists.
provisions.notes: No exclusion is asserted by the question.

provisions.quotation: Employees shall not input sensitive or proprietary information about students, colleagues, or institutional operations into AI systems that lack safeguards and policies to protect such data from being used in their training models, and if such sensitive or proprietary information will be entered into an AI system, employees shall seek the approval of their Principal before doing so.
provisions.scope: Sensitive or proprietary student information entered into AI systems
provisions.conditions: No entry into systems lacking safeguards/policies against training reuse; Principal approval must also be sought before sensitive input.
provisions.notes: District class denotes explicitly named Principal. Approval is for input, not a waiver allowing training; do not chart as training allowed with Principal consent.

provisions.quotation: Complete a Privacy Impact Assessment before using AI with these data. Prefer aggregated or de-identified data, include AI clauses in contracts, and never train AI with student data unless approved.
provisions.scope: Student data used to train AI
provisions.conditions: Training only if approved; complete PIA before AI use; aggregated/de-identified data preferred.
provisions.notes: Passive approved does not identify approver.

provisions.quotation: Student data stays protected — Approved enterprise AI tools do not use OCPS data to train public AI models, and sensitive information may only be entered into tools approved for that type of data.
provisions.scope: OCPS data in approved enterprise tools for public AI model training
provisions.conditions: Only approved enterprise tools; only public models.
provisions.notes: Sensitive-input permission not interpreted as permission to train.

provisions.quotation: Enterprise Tools — Staff use District-vetted, secure AI systems that do not use OCPS data to train public models.
provisions.actor: District-vetted secure AI systems used by staff
provisions.scope: OCPS data for public models in District-vetted tools
provisions.conditions: District-vetted secure systems only.
provisions.notes: Scoped assurance, not a ban on all internal-model training.

provisions.quotation: Google Gemini and Adobe Express with Firefly were selected because they meet needed cybersecurity and privacy requirements and each vendor has an executed contract with the School District. Each provider has agreed to the District’s privacy terms that the data input into and generated by these tools will be housed exclusively in the United States, that data will not be sold or shared without permission to third parties, and that data input into these tools will not be used to train their AI models:
provisions.actor: Contracted Google Gemini and Adobe Express with Firefly providers
provisions.scope: Data input into the two contracted tools for their AI-model training
provisions.conditions: Scope limited to executed district contracts and named tools.
provisions.notes: Sharing permission exception applies only to sale/sharing, not training. Training sentence covers inputs, not automatically generated data.

provisions.quotation: Information entered into, uploaded to, or generated by approved tools through a District-provided account is not used to train or improve AI models.
provisions.scope: Entered, uploaded or generated information through District-provided approved-tool accounts
provisions.conditions: District-provided account required for assurance.
provisions.notes: Training and improvement of AI models are one model-training purpose, not separate generic service-improvement provisions.

provisions.quotation: When used with district accounts, Gemini provides enterprise-grade security, and your data is not used to train AI models.
provisions.scope: Data in district-account Gemini
provisions.conditions: District-account use only.
provisions.notes: Recommendation to choose Gemini is not authorization for training.

provisions.quotation: The vetting process shall include a review of the tool’s privacy policy, data storage practices, training and data policies, and compliance with FERPA.
provisions.scope: AI tool training and data policies
provisions.conditions: Review during vetting.
provisions.notes: Training-policy review does not establish a substantive no-training term.

provisions.quotation: When using any AI tool, especially free ones, consider turning off the chat history. This way, your students' conversations won't be saved or used to train the AI.
provisions.scope: Students' conversations in AI tools, especially free ones
provisions.conditions: Consider disabling chat history; source claims this prevents saving and training.
provisions.notes: Technical claim not independently validated; no equation of retention with training adopted by reviewer.

provisions.quotation: Some platforms may also retain prompts, uploaded content, or user interactions to train models or improve system performance, which highlights the need for rigorous vendor review processes.
provisions.scope: Prompts, uploads and user interactions retained for model training
provisions.conditions: Possibility for some platforms; vendor review needed.
provisions.notes: Training risk only; system-performance improvement separately coded T032.

provisions.quotation: Some platforms may also retain prompts, uploaded content, or user interactions to train models or improve system performance, which highlights the need for rigorous vendor review processes.
provisions.scope: Prompts, uploads and user interactions retained for system-performance improvement
provisions.conditions: Possibility for some platforms; vendor review needed.
provisions.notes: Distinct purpose from model training; shared exact quotation preserves the alternative purposes without transferring a ban.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] This law and its amendments and rules include the right to know what data is being collected to train AI models and how data is being used/shared.
provisions.actor: Entities collecting data under source's CCPA summary
provisions.scope: Disclosure of data collected to train AI models
provisions.conditions: Source describes a right to know, not a right to train or a training ban.
provisions.notes: Legal summary is source content, not independently validated authority; student-specific applicability not established by this sentence.

provisions.quotation: This is especially pertinent when using open AI tools since data imputed into open AI is reshared to train the AI model. This resharing of data is a violation of FERPA, meaning that personally identifiable student information should never be shared outside of a closed system without parental/eligible student consent. All student information used in open AI systems should be anonymized to prevent a violation of FERPA.
provisions.actor: Schools and users of open AI tools
provisions.scope: Student information in open AI tools; warning about resharing for training
provisions.conditions: Source recommends anonymization; parental/eligible-student consent condition concerns identifiable-data disclosure outside closed systems.
provisions.notes: Source's broad FERPA and training claims not independently validated. No training permission inferred from disclosure consent; authorizers not duplicated as training permissions.

provisions.quotation: • Does the vendor use personal data to train or improve its AI models?
provisions.scope: Personal data for vendor AI-model training or improvement
provisions.conditions: Ask in tool-vetting review.
provisions.notes: Question, not a prohibition; model improvement remains model training.

provisions.quotation: To protect student privacy, only AI tools that have been officially vetted and approved, which guarantee that student data is not used to train the AI mode and comply with all applicable privacy laws (e.g. FERPA, COPPA) may be used.
provisions.actor: AI tools eligible for district student use
provisions.scope: Student data in officially vetted and approved tools for AI-model training
provisions.conditions: No-training guarantee and compliance are prerequisites to tool use.
provisions.notes: Source typo AI mode preserved; approved-tool use permission is not permission to train.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] Training Protocols and Data Policy: • [graphic] Protection of user generated data, including ensuring that vendors are not leveraging student data for model training, product improvement or purposes outside of the contracted service.
provisions.scope: Student data for vendor model training
provisions.conditions: Representative considerations prior to procurement; ensuring nonuse is a selection consideration.
provisions.notes: Not converted to mandatory operative prohibition; product improvement separately coded T038.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] Training Protocols and Data Policy: • [graphic] Protection of user generated data, including ensuring that vendors are not leveraging student data for model training, product improvement or purposes outside of the contracted service.
provisions.scope: Student data for vendor product improvement
provisions.conditions: Representative considerations prior to procurement; source lists product improvement separately from purposes outside contracted service.
provisions.notes: Do not invent an in-contract improvement exception from the disjunctive list; no operative permission.

provisions.quotation: • Prioritize privacy: Never share personal information with AI models and be aware that user data may be used to train these models.
provisions.scope: Student/user information supplied to AI models
provisions.conditions: Be aware of possible training use; surrounding student guidance uses should.
provisions.notes: Never-share instruction is about input, not evidence that training is permitted or universally performed.

provisions.quotation: Key Questions: Procurement and Vendor Management (page 59) • Explain how vendors are vetted regarding AI model training, data handling, and equity or accessibility safeguards. What questions or criteria are used?
provisions.scope: Vendor AI-model training practices in procurement
provisions.conditions: Explain vetting questions/criteria.
provisions.notes: Reflection prompt, not mandatory no-training contract language.

provisions.quotation: Currently, the only one of the large frontier model companies that provides an education version of their Large Language Model is Google’s, which now provides their Gemini 3 for all Google Workspace for Education users with enhanced data privacy including no training on chats.
provisions.actor: Google Gemini 3 for Workspace for Education
provisions.scope: Chats of Google Workspace for Education users in identified Gemini offering
provisions.conditions: Education offering only; source's current product characterization.
provisions.notes: No external verification of product availability or claim. Separate age/use recommendations are not training exceptions.

provisions.quotation: New AI tools not only process typed inputs but can now accept voice recordings, images, and even location data. These inputs are often stored by vendors for model training or product improvement, even when students or staff assume the data is private.
provisions.scope: Typed and multimodal inputs, including voice, images and location, used for model training
provisions.conditions: Source says often, not invariably; applies even when users assume privacy.
provisions.notes: Training risk separate from product-improvement risk T043.

provisions.quotation: New AI tools not only process typed inputs but can now accept voice recordings, images, and even location data. These inputs are often stored by vendors for model training or product improvement, even when students or staff assume the data is private.
provisions.scope: Typed and multimodal inputs used for product improvement
provisions.conditions: Source says often, not invariably; user assumption of privacy does not ensure nonuse.
provisions.notes: Distinct purpose, not inferred from all AI-model improvement wording.

provisions.quotation: LLM models such as ChatGPT utilize user input in the form of chats to continue training the models. Therefore it is imperative that users fully understand NOT to enter, paste, or upload any PII into the chat of any generative AI tool.
provisions.scope: Chats containing PII used for continued LLM training
provisions.conditions: Warns against PII input; next paragraph allows input only into vetted, approved, locally integrated tools.
provisions.notes: Source's general ChatGPT training statement not independently endorsed. Input exception is not a model-training permission.

provisions.quotation: PSUs should understand how each product or tool harvests data for training and continual learning. This is critical to help ensure sensitive data or contaminated data is not ingested.
provisions.scope: Product/tool data harvesting for training and continual learning
provisions.conditions: Understand harvesting to protect sensitive/contaminated data.
provisions.notes: Adjacent must-audit requirement does not turn should-understand into a training prohibition.

provisions.quotation: • Avoid Model Training on School Data
provisions.scope: School data for model training
provisions.conditions: Avoidance item within pre-adoption security-audit checklist.
provisions.notes: Avoid wording coded as recommended exclusion; not unconditional mandatory shall-not wording. Simulated-data pilot item is not itself a training authorization.

provisions.quotation: Users, both school staff and students, should be cautious when entering any personal information into any and all digital applications, including generative AI tools. Entering Personally Identifiable Information (PII) into any generative AI system should always be avoided. This is a particularly important consideration when using generative AI applications such as ChatGPT, as the information entered by users (including prompts and questions posed, etc.) is stored on the application’s server and integrated into the large language model used to respond to user prompts. Essentially, generative AI tools are learning from every single piece of text or other input typed into their platforms.
provisions.scope: Personal inputs and prompts in generative AI applications
provisions.conditions: Avoid PII input. Following B022 qualifies generalization with private/education-version vendor no-training claims that cannot be independently verified.
provisions.notes: Warning, not permission; source's assertion equating all input with learning is not reviewer validation.

provisions.quotation: While this statement generally still holds true as of the most recent release of this guidance document, many genAI tools are now offering a 'private mode' and/or education versions in which the companies that own then state that they are not retaining data for model training, though this cannot be independently verified.
provisions.actor: Companies offering private-mode or education GenAI versions
provisions.scope: Data retained for training in private-mode and/or education versions
provisions.conditions: Vendor-stated claim; source expressly says cannot be independently verified.
provisions.notes: Does not guarantee all private/education products exclude training or that retention and training are equivalent.

provisions.quotation: Entering PII into generative AI tools should always be avoided, as this information is often stored on the tool’s servers and used to train the AI model. This poses risks of violating privacy regulations like FERPA, creating legal consequences, and damaging trust. Only district approved AI tools, like Gemini, should be used.
provisions.scope: PII entered into generative AI tools
provisions.conditions: Avoid PII input and use approved tools; training described as often, not always.
provisions.notes: No inference that approval authorizes training or guarantees nonuse.

provisions.quotation: Information entered into generative AI systems or integrated into existing digital resources can be stored and used for training purposes, leading to risks of data breaches, misuse, or unintended harvesting (oversharing).
provisions.actor: Generative AI systems and integrated digital resources
provisions.scope: Information entered into GenAI or integrated digital resources
provisions.conditions: Potential storage and training use; surrounding context concerns confidential student information.
provisions.notes: Can denotes possible risk, not permission.

provisions.quotation: • Privacy by default - strict prohibition on using data for training models without explicit consent.
provisions.scope: Data used for model training in student/staff privacy considerations
provisions.conditions: Explicit consent exception; consent-giver unspecified.
provisions.notes: Strict prohibition is normative wording but appears in considerations, not independently established law. Adjacent unless-required input clauses are not training exceptions.

provisions.quotation: • Insist on vendor transparency regarding data sources and model training procedures
provisions.scope: Vendor data sources and model-training procedures
provisions.conditions: Procurement-checklist transparency consideration.
provisions.notes: Does not explicitly require no training; student-data connection is procurement context, not a claim that all training sources are student data.

provisions.quotation: District-approved tools have been vetted to ensure data privacy requirements are met. This ensures your information is not used to train AI models and that data is not shared publicly.
provisions.scope: Information in district-approved tools
provisions.conditions: District-approved tools only.
provisions.notes: Vetting assurance not externally verified; public sharing separate from training.

provisions.quotation: Is student data being used to train AI models? No. For our approved Google Workspace Core Services (Gemini and NotebookLM), student chats, prompts, and uploaded files are never used to train AI models and are never shared outside the district.
provisions.actor: Approved Google Workspace Core Services (Gemini and NotebookLM)
provisions.scope: Student chats, prompts and uploads in named approved Core Services
provisions.conditions: Named district-approved Google services only.
provisions.notes: Never-used assurance, not independent verification or ban covering personal Google accounts.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Privacy: Students understand that LLMs may use any information the students provide to train future models and that once personal information is shared, its privacy cannot be assured.
provisions.actor: Students learning AI literacy; LLM providers
provisions.scope: Information students provide to LLMs for future-model training
provisions.conditions: May-use risk statement; no guarantee of privacy after sharing.
provisions.notes: Literacy warning, not a school's training authorization.

provisions.quotation: Approved vendors must demonstrate compliance with the District’s privacy and data handling standards, including a commitment to not using District data to train external models unless explicitly permitted.
provisions.scope: District data for external-model training
provisions.conditions: Explicit permission exception; commitment must be demonstrated.
provisions.notes: No authorizer named; District standards do not establish who grants permission.

provisions.quotation: • Students have the right to protect their personal data and creative works from unauthorized AI training or exploitation while using district-provided AI tools.
provisions.actor: District-provided AI tools and data users
provisions.scope: Student personal data and creative works in district-provided AI tools
provisions.conditions: Protection against unauthorized training; authorized training conditions and authorizer not stated.
provisions.notes: Rights wording is normative. Student right to protection does not explicitly make student the training authorizer; exploitation not separately coded as improvement.

provisions.quotation: • Use of user's data to train new Al Systems: Baldwin County Public Schools will include in our procurement and contract document(s) verbiage dedicated to usage of intellectual property and/or data, to which the Contractor shall attest when submitting their proposals and any contract executed to perform the work.
provisions.actor: Baldwin County Public Schools and Contractor
provisions.scope: User data/intellectual property for training new AI systems
provisions.conditions: Include dedicated contract/procurement wording; contractor attestation in proposals and executed contract.
provisions.notes: Does not state the substance of a training ban here. Source Al spelling preserved.

provisions.quotation: • The Al model(s) have been pre-trained and no data is being used to train a model to be used in the development of a new product.
provisions.scope: Data training a model for development of new product
provisions.conditions: Previous paragraph requires district to obtain written contractor statement.
provisions.notes: Attestation content, not no training for every purpose; source Al spelling preserved.

provisions.quotation: When using GenAI tools, it is crucial to understand that any information provided whether through prompts entered by the user or AI-generated responses could potentially be used by companies to train their models. This includes personal details of students, families, employees, and any proprietary or confidential information belonging to Bentonville Schools. Assume that all information shared with a GenAI application will be used to train the model and could become accessible in the public domain.
provisions.scope: User prompts and AI-generated responses, including student details and district confidential information
provisions.conditions: Potential training use; precautionary assume-all-information instruction.
provisions.notes: Precautionary risk assumption not verified assertion of all products' behavior. Outputs coded only because source expressly identifies them as training inputs.

provisions.quotation: Students are prohibited from using any AI tools that collect and employ user data to train or improve their underlying models. The training of learning models is strictly limited to a classroom setting when it is part of the curriculum instruction on model training, and the model must be managed by the teacher (not utilizing external public data or services).
provisions.actor: Students and teacher managing classroom model
provisions.scope: AI tools collecting/employing user data to train or improve underlying models; classroom instructional training
provisions.conditions: Training limited to classroom curriculum instruction, with teacher-managed model and no external public data/services.
provisions.notes: Teacher management is an explicit condition, not a named consent/authorization grant. External-tool exclusion and curricular exception coded together.

provisions.quotation: • Data Ownership: District data remains District property and cannot be used by vendors to train public AI models. To ensure compliance with this principle, contracts must include language noting this requirement.
provisions.scope: District data for public AI model training
provisions.conditions: Contract language must implement restriction; public models only.
provisions.notes: Ownership statement and implementation duty support same training restriction; not duplicated.

provisions.quotation: Microsoft Copilot (tool card) • An AI assistant inside the district's protected Microsoft environment, with enterprise data protection enabled. • Enterprise data protection enabled • Not used to train public AI models on school data
provisions.actor: Microsoft Copilot in protected district environment
provisions.scope: School data for public AI model training in Copilot
provisions.conditions: District protected Microsoft environment with enterprise data protection enabled.
provisions.notes: Scoped tool-card assurance, not all Copilot accounts or all model training.

provisions.quotation: MagicSchool AI (tool card) • Student data is never used to train AI models, and the district owns all of it
provisions.scope: Student data in listed MagicSchool AI offering
provisions.conditions: Approved district tool-card context.
provisions.notes: No public-model qualifier appears in this clause; ownership is not a separate training permission.

provisions.quotation: Based on current district requirements and practices, student information entered into approved tools must remain within the Broward County Public Schools environment; student information is not used to train district-approved Artificial Intelligence models.
provisions.scope: Student information entered into approved Broward tools for district-approved model training
provisions.conditions: Current district requirements/practices; approved tools only.
provisions.notes: Must remain controls location; training clause is descriptive is not used. Do not transfer must across the semicolon.

provisions.quotation: 22. Do student interactions train the Artificial Intelligence models? No. Under current district requirements, approved Broward County Public Schools tools must not use our students’ interactions to train Artificial Intelligence models.
provisions.actor: Approved Broward County Public Schools tools
provisions.scope: Students' interactions in approved Broward tools
provisions.conditions: Current district requirements; approved tools only.
provisions.notes: Explicit must-not restriction; no extrapolation to external unapproved products.

provisions.quotation: Under current district requirements, student information in approved tools must remain within the Broward County Public Schools environment and cannot be used to train Artificial Intelligence models.
provisions.scope: Student information in approved district tools
provisions.conditions: Current district requirements; district-approved tools.
provisions.notes: Myth headline excluded so quotation does not falsely assert training occurs.

provisions.quotation: No. Approved tools are configured so student and staff information is not used to train public AI models. This is a condition of approval for every tool listed on this site.
provisions.actor: Approved tools listed on district site
provisions.scope: Student and staff information for public AI model training
provisions.conditions: No public-model training is explicit approval condition for listed tools.
provisions.notes: Configuration assurance attached to normative approval criterion; not an assurance for tools outside list.

provisions.quotation: Open-Source Generative AI Systems (Not Secure) These are AI tools that operate on publicly accessible platforms or models, often provided by third-party vendors. Example: ChatGPT (free/public version), Claude (free/public version), and other web-based tools where data entered may be used to train future models. Data entered is typically stored and may be used by the provider unless explicitly stated otherwise.
provisions.scope: Entered data in described free/public web tools for future-model training
provisions.conditions: Possible training use; explicit provider statements may say otherwise.
provisions.notes: Source's open-source label not technically validated. May-use and unless-stated-otherwise do not constitute granted permission.

provisions.quotation: Closed-Source Generative AI Systems (Secure) These systems operate within a controlled, private environment. Example: Microsoft Copilot with Microsoft 365. Data is not used to train models and remains protected within the organization’s secure environment.
provisions.actor: Systems in source's controlled/private environment example
provisions.scope: Data within controlled private systems, exemplified by Microsoft Copilot with Microsoft 365
provisions.conditions: Controlled/private organizational environment as described by source.
provisions.notes: Not a verified generic property of all closed-source models; public/private terminology is source characterization.

provisions.quotation: When using GenAI tools, it is crucial to understand that any information provided—whether through prompts entered by the user or AI-generated responses—could potentially be used by companies to train their models unless that company has an approved data privacy agreement with the District. This includes stakeholders’ personal details, and any proprietary or confidential information belonging to CPS. Assume that all information shared with a GenAI application will be used to train the model and could become accessible in the public domain unless explicitly told otherwise.
provisions.scope: Prompts, generated responses and stakeholder/district confidential information shared with GenAI
provisions.conditions: Potential-use warning excepts companies with approved District DPAs; precautionary assumption applies unless explicitly told otherwise.
provisions.notes: DPA qualification limits warning, not explicit training authorization. Includes outputs only because source identifies them as potential training data.

provisions.quotation: As a further precaution, staff are advised to turn off chat history and data training in the settings of any GenAI tool used in their professional practice.
provisions.scope: Data-training setting of any professionally used GenAI tool
provisions.conditions: Advised setting disablement as further precaution.
provisions.notes: Not mandatory; disabling history not assumed sufficient without disabling training. Separate confidential-entry DPA requirement excluded.

provisions.quotation: Foundational model vendors must ensure that stakeholder information, copyrighted material, or proprietary CPS intellectual property is not used to train their models without explicit permission.
provisions.scope: Stakeholder information, copyrighted material and proprietary CPS IP for foundational model training
provisions.conditions: Explicit permission exception; permission-giver not stated.
provisions.notes: Do not assume District or copyright owner is authorizer solely from ownership labels.

provisions.quotation: Foundational model vendors must ensure that stakeholder information, copyrighted material, or proprietary CPS intellectual property is not used to train their models without explicit permission. Application layer vendors must ensure that the same is not used in the fine-tuning of their tools or shared with the foundational model vendor without explicit permission.
provisions.scope: Stakeholder information, copyrighted material and proprietary CPS IP for application-layer fine-tuning
provisions.conditions: Explicit permission exception; related onward sharing also requires explicit permission.
provisions.notes: First sentence retained only to resolve the same antecedent. Distinct application fine-tuning duty, not duplicate foundational-training provision. Sharing alone not labeled training.

provisions.quotation: Approved tools have entered into an enterprise data share agreement, meaning they have a contract with CPS agreeing not to train their models on or store any data from interactions with their product–ensuring student privacy.
provisions.scope: Data from interactions with products under CPS enterprise agreement
provisions.conditions: Approved tools' contract with CPS.
provisions.notes: Explicit contractual no-training promise; storage prohibition is separate purpose and not a second training record.

provisions.quotation: SchoolAI has contracted agreements with large language model providers such as OpenAI and Microsoft that ensure personal student data is not saved or used by third-parties to train or refine future models.
provisions.actor: Third-party LLM providers contracted with SchoolAI
provisions.scope: Personal student data for third-party future-model training or refinement
provisions.conditions: SchoolAI provider agreements; third parties only.
provisions.notes: Explicit contractual assurance; does not establish every internal SchoolAI use is excluded.

provisions.quotation: There shall be no use of district data for training new products without prior written DCS approval and documented scope.
provisions.scope: District data for training new products
provisions.conditions: Prior written DCS approval and documented scope.
provisions.notes: No blanket prohibition; separate data-access agreement not treated as the training approval itself.

provisions.quotation: • The AI model(s) have been pretrained, and no data is being used to train a model to be used in the development of a new product;
provisions.scope: Data for model training to develop a new product
provisions.conditions: Written-statement collection required in preceding paragraph; B015/B026 allow scoped district-approved uses.
provisions.notes: Current no-new-product-training representation; not ban on all future district-specific training.

provisions.quotation: The Contractor hereby attests and agrees that it is expressly prohibited from using any data provided to it by the data providers—either in its raw form or after undergoing any form of processing, aggregation, or transformation—for the purpose of training a new AI System to be used in a new product, model, service, or offering (collectively referred to as the "Product") of the Contractor.
provisions.scope: Provider-supplied raw, processed, aggregated or transformed data for new contractor-product AI training
provisions.conditions: Express notwithstanding exception in B025-B026 allows district-required customization/new-system development for District-Specific Needs with prior written DCS approval and compliance with law and contract.
provisions.notes: Quote contains restriction only; exception in separate source paragraph coded T080. Not an unconditional ban; cross-paragraph qualification cannot be included in contiguous quotation.

provisions.quotation: • Customize the AI System currently in use, which may result in the development of a new AI System. • Develop a new AI System. The customization and development of the AI System is expressly required by the Dothan City School District to meet the specific needs of the School District (the "District-Specific Needs"). Any such use of the data for the district-specific needs shall be subject to prior written approval by the Dothan City School District and shall be carried out in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, and the terms and conditions of this contract.
provisions.scope: Provider data for district-specific customization/new-system development
provisions.conditions: Expressly required by DCS for District-Specific Needs; prior written DCS approval; applicable laws, regulations and contract. Preceding notwithstanding clause establishes exception.
provisions.notes: One approval regime covering both enumerated activities; not general contractor-product training permission.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot are powered by OpenAI’s GPT models while Google Gemini is powered by Google’s Gemini models. These generative AI tools sit within the Houston ISD domain. They are enterprise generative AI tools, which means that chat history is not used to train the models.
provisions.actor: District-domain enterprise ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini
provisions.scope: Chat history in identified Houston ISD enterprise environments
provisions.conditions: Houston ISD domain enterprise versions only.
provisions.notes: No generalization to consumer accounts or all enterprise offerings; tool recommendation not permission to train.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] Microsoft 365 Copilot — Rationale for Selection: This generative AI tool sits within the Houston ISD domain and plugs into the Microsoft suite of productivity tools including Word, Powerpoint, Teams, and Outlook. Through the plug-in, the tool has access to all data stored within the Microsoft suite of programs and can answer questions using that data as an input. It is an enterprise generative AI tool, which means that any sensitive data that is shared with this tool does not get shared back with the AI for training purposes.
provisions.actor: Microsoft 365 Copilot in Houston ISD domain
provisions.scope: Sensitive data shared with district-domain Microsoft 365 Copilot
provisions.conditions: Named district enterprise environment.
provisions.notes: Answering questions from suite data is not counted as training; last sentence explicitly distinguishes training reuse.

provisions.quotation: Houston ISD provides access to secure, district-managed AI environments, including the enterprise version of Google Gemini for staff and students ages 13 and older. These tools do not use student or staff data to train external AI models and operate within HISD’s security and privacy requirements, including access controls, monitoring, and safeguards designed to prevent the exposure or misuse of sensitive information.
provisions.actor: Secure district-managed Houston ISD AI tools
provisions.scope: Student/staff data in district-managed tools for external-model training
provisions.conditions: District-managed environments; named enterprise Gemini access is for staff and students 13 and older.
provisions.notes: External-model assurance only; no inference about every internal training use.

provisions.quotation: Therefore, district users must avoid inputting sensitive, confidential, proprietary, or copyrighted materials into AI platforms unless the AI provider explicitly confirms compliance with Education Law 2-d and guarantees that input information will not be reused for future AI model training, as well as other standard compliance factors including how information is stored and transmitted on the servers that host the platform or service.
provisions.scope: Sensitive, confidential, proprietary or copyrighted input, including student work in paragraph context
provisions.conditions: Input boundary requires explicit provider law-compliance confirmation and no-future-model-training guarantee plus standard storage/transmission compliance.
provisions.notes: Conditional protected-input rule requires no training; provider guarantee is not permission to train, and no authorizer is named.

provisions.quotation: Information input into GenAI tools that have not been approved by the District may be used for algorithm training and made available to other users of the system outside the district.
provisions.actor: GenAI tools not approved by District
provisions.scope: Information input into unapproved GenAI tools for algorithm training
provisions.conditions: Unapproved tools; may-use warning.
provisions.notes: Adjacent PII-entry prohibition does not establish approved tools never train.

provisions.quotation: When using enterprise accounts, ensure that data protection includes safeguards to ensure that prompts and responses are not used to train foundation models.
provisions.scope: Enterprise-account prompts/responses for foundation-model training
provisions.conditions: Ensure nonuse safeguards for enterprise accounts; paragraph presents local-review guidance.
provisions.notes: Recommended safeguard check, not proof safeguard exists. Responses are included as explicit potential training data.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Is there confirmation that identifiable student, employee, or user data is not used for model training, product improvement, analytics, or future AI model development unless expressly authorized through the school system’s legal/privacy process? Can the school system opt out of model training or secondary data use?
provisions.scope: Identifiable student, employee or user data for model training/future AI model development
provisions.conditions: Ask confirmation of nonuse unless expressly authorized through school-system legal/privacy process; ask whether school system can opt out.
provisions.notes: Questions not enacted permission or ban. District authorizer class reflects explicitly named school-system process; no guessed individual approver. Analytics excluded as separate practice.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Is there confirmation that identifiable student, employee, or user data is not used for model training, product improvement, analytics, or future AI model development unless expressly authorized through the school system’s legal/privacy process? Can the school system opt out of model training or secondary data use?
provisions.scope: Identifiable student, employee or user data for product improvement
provisions.conditions: Ask confirmation of nonuse except express authorization through school-system legal/privacy process; inquire about secondary-use opt-out.
provisions.notes: Product improvement separately named. No general analytics use inferred to be improvement, and no actual opt-out right asserted.

provisions.quotation: AI vendors must meet strict privacy, security, and transparency standards. Districts must ensure contractual limits on data use, retention, and deletion; prohibit advertising, profiling, or unrelated model training; require disclosure of data practices; and ensure compliance with breach notification laws.
provisions.scope: Unrelated model training by AI vendors using covered district data
provisions.conditions: Restriction specifically limited to unrelated model training.
provisions.notes: No implication that related training is permitted. Advertising and profiling are not training provisions.

provisions.quotation: Vendors must provide clear documentation on AI techniques, data collection and retention, use of data for model training, known limitations, accessibility and nondiscrimination measures, and evaluation populations. Tools that lack sufficient transparency must not be adopted.
provisions.scope: Vendor documentation of data use for model training
provisions.conditions: Clear documentation required; insufficiently transparent tools must not be adopted.
provisions.notes: Mandatory transparency, not mandatory prohibition of training.

provisions.quotation: • Response: On the LEA level, LEAs should not allow their data or information to be used to train the vendor’s models. This can be negotiated with the vendor. Know how your data will be used.
provisions.scope: LEA data/information used to train vendor models
provisions.conditions: Should-not-allow recommendation; negotiate with vendor.
provisions.notes: Recommended no-training term, not mandatory law or evidence of negotiated term already in effect.

provisions.quotation: • Explicit written vendor confirmation that student data is not utilized to train public or proprietary AI models without explicit, non-standard consent.
provisions.scope: Student data for public or proprietary AI model training
provisions.conditions: Seek explicit written vendor confirmation of nonuse absent explicit non-standard consent.
provisions.notes: Procurement checklist criterion, not actual consent or blanket ban. Consent-giver unspecified; non-standard consent retained without inventing definition.

provisions.quotation: • Overview: Generative AI tools introduce severe data privacy risks, as consumer-facing prompts are often retained by vendors to train future models.
provisions.scope: Consumer-facing prompts retained for future-model training
provisions.conditions: Often, not invariably; consumer tier.
provisions.notes: Risk warning; subsequent recommended zero-retention and PII controls do not enact an all-model training prohibition.

provisions.quotation: [graphic] Vendors are prohibited from using Division data for AI model training or algorithm development. AI tools shall not reuse, sell, or employ data for model training or secondary purposes without explicit written consent from the Division and, when applicable, from parents or guardians.
provisions.scope: Division data for AI model training/algorithm development; AI-tool training reuse
provisions.conditions: First sentence prohibits vendors' training/algorithm development; following sentence requires explicit written Division consent AND parent/guardian consent when applicable for training/secondary use. Whether the exception overrides first sentence's vendor ban is not resolved.
provisions.notes: District enum denotes Division; additional explicit parent authorizer retained conjunctively in conditions to avoid duplicate permission records. Scope tension warrants chart flag; never present as unconditional prohibition or unrestricted Division-only permission. Sale/secondary purposes not automatically service improvement.

provisions.quotation: Staff and students may request that their personal data not be used for AI training or automated decision-making systems. Requests for data access, correction, or opt-out shall follow procedures established under FERPA and Division data-access protocols.
provisions.actor: Staff and students making requests; Division processing them
provisions.scope: Staff/student personal data requested to be excluded from AI training
provisions.conditions: May request nonuse; requests follow FERPA and Division data-access procedures.
provisions.notes: Right to request, not guarantee of fulfillment, deletion, or training authorization. Student is requester, not expressly training authorizer. Automated decision-making not coded as training.

provisions.quotation: • [graphic] Verify that: • [graphic] Data are encrypted in transit and at rest. • [graphic] Servers are hosted in the United States. • [graphic] The vendor provides clear data usage and retention policies. • [graphic] Vendor data are not used to train proprietary models or for commercial purposes. • [graphic] Tools failing privacy or security standards shall be rejected or flagged for remediation by Technology Services and Legal.
provisions.scope: Literal vendor data used for proprietary-model training in tool privacy review
provisions.conditions: Verify nonuse; failing tools rejected OR flagged for remediation.
provisions.notes: Context is PII/Division tool vetting, but literal vendor data does not clearly specify student data. Do not silently rewrite possessive scope or treat verification item as standalone all-training ban; explicit consent regime in B017 remains relevant.

provisions.quotation: AI systems, not vetted by school districts, may be training their AI model using data from chat conversations.
provisions.actor: AI systems not vetted by school districts
provisions.scope: Chat conversations in unvetted AI systems
provisions.conditions: May-be-training risk; unvetted systems.
provisions.notes: Student intellectual-property heading supplies educational relevance; not a claim approved tools categorically cannot train.

provisions.quotation: In addition, generative AI uses data to train AI systems, and schools should be concerned about the intellectual property of students being utilized to train these systems.
provisions.scope: Student intellectual property used for AI-system training
provisions.conditions: Schools should be concerned about training reuse.
provisions.notes: Concern not an operative ban; separate FERPA/COPPA compliance wording does not establish specific training treatment.

provisions.quotation: It is not enough to remove student-identifiable information before submitting student work to an AI system. This still exposes the student’s intellectual property to the system. SU/SDs should have a privacy agreement with vendors that include promises not to train AI models based on chat conversations. This is the case for education-specific AI systems as well as generic systems with AI versions (Gemini for Education).
provisions.scope: Chat conversations including student work/IP in education-specific and generic AI offerings
provisions.conditions: Recommended privacy agreement with vendor no-training promises; removing student identifiers alone insufficient.
provisions.notes: Recommended contract restriction, not evidence agreement exists or automatic permission for de-identified work.

provisions.quotation: Obtaining parental consent is crucial, but it is also important to recognize that even with consent, using identifiable data in public AI models is not advisable. Any data information inputted into the AI model, including prompts, has the potential to be incorporated into the model’s future iterations and potentially shared with other users.
provisions.scope: Identifiable student data and prompts in public AI models, potentially incorporated into future iterations
provisions.conditions: Use remains not advisable even with parental consent; incorporation/sharing framed as potential.
provisions.notes: Parental consent is not construed as explicit training authorization. Warning not unconditional legal ban; source's future-incorporation risk supports training classification.
